title: U.S. Finds A War It’s Willing to Declare

The Department of Homeland Security has decided that the agency needs a new
official seal. Where the ubiquitous American eagle faced the direction of the
olive branches in its right talon, now the eagle will face the opposite
direction -- towards the arrows it clasps in its other talon.

"We're actually changing our seal to make it look towards the arrows because …
when it looks towards the arrows is when it means we're at war," Secretary
Markwayne Mullin [revealed](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BPs5M5JAh2Q) in a
Fox News interview this weekend. "Homeland Security is at war every single day
against bad actors trying to hurt our backyards, and we're not gonna allow
that to happen."

So in other words, the United States is at war here at home -- but Iran
somehow [isn't](https://x.com/cspan/status/2095948691727106239?s=20) a war.
What?

In October 1945, seven weeks after the Japanese surrender in World War II,
President Harry Truman issued Executive Order 9646, the first order in
American history to define the great seal in legal language, with the eagle's
head codified as facing toward the olive branch. Truman said it was to reflect
the new world of peace. Churchill quipped: "Why not put the eagle's neck on a
swivel so that it could turn to the right or left as the occasion presented
itself?"

Nearly a century later, Churchill's vision won out.

" If you look at most of our seals throughout all the agencies, the eagle
looks to the palm leaf because that's in a time of peace," Mullin said in the
interview.

If anything, Mullin is underselling the significance. _All_ federal agencies'
seals depict the peacetime eagle facing the palm leaf, not just "most." And
not only has Homeland never before depicted the wartime posture (not even
after 9/11) -- _no_ U.S. agency has since World War II. Not even the
"Department of War"!

There's something very creepy about our government seeing America as a
battlefield in ways it doesn't even see overseas.

"The Department of Homeland Security seal was created in June 2003 and is
symbolic of the Department's mission -- to prevent attacks and protect
Americans -- on the land, in the sea and in the air," DHS officially
[says](https://www.dhs.gov/department-homeland-security-seal) of the now
obsolete eagle.__ The meaning was pretty straightforward: protect America from
external threats.

Which raises the question of who, exactly, DHS believes itself to be at war
with. Mullin's public answer is the standard list -- Islamic terrorists,
cartels, weapons of mass destruction, etc. -- but he keeps returning to the
war being against Americans domestically.

"Free speech is something we all protect, but there's a line that you can
cross that goes from free speech to inciting dangerous behavior; and we have
to attack that dangerous behavior at every turning point," Mullin told Fox
News.

This war against free speech is not just rhetoric. The federal government is
increasingly monitoring what Americans say, particularly on social media, and
it is increasingly building AI tools to monitor everything and flag what it
considers threatening or offensive for further investigation.

FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia recently revealed key details of the
machinery behind this in a little-noticed
[interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fEhMLy-0ABM) this weekend.

Of dangerous speech, he says: "Obviously, huge uptick the last year, 18
months, in political violence, political rhetoric, government violence, crime
against the government -- you name it, whether it's FBI agents, ICE agents,
congressmen on both sides of the aisle."

The FBI is combatting this, Raia says, with National Security Presidential
Memorandum 7, which [I've explained
here](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/trumps-nspm-7-labels-common-beliefs).

NSPM-7, signed by Trump last September, directs the federal government to
disrupt "organized political violence" -- and lists, among the indicators that
someone might be inclined toward it, "anti-Americanism," "anti-capitalism,"
"anti-Christianity," and "extremism on migration, race, and gender." In other
words, speech.

If you have any doubts about whether it's really war, listen to Raia compare
the methodology of NSPM-7 and its newly created "Joint Mission Center" to
external (non) war:

> "You're familiar with the way that we worked the Iranian threat. We kinda
> did the same thing the way we worked the Iranian threat, and we applied it
> to this threat."

Think about that for a sec. The bureau's response to Iran's domestic pot-
stirring has entailed network mapping, informant recruitment, financial
tracing, FISA collection, and pretextual interviews designed to rattle a
target and see what falls out. It was built to counter the clandestine
operations of a foreign adversary.

Now, this apparatus is being pointed at Americans.

And it has been staffed accordingly. Raia describes pulling personnel out of
the divisions that normally have nothing to do with one another:

> "There are pieces of this threat that encompasses our criminal division.
> There are pieces of this threat that encompasses the cyber division. There's
> pieces that encompass CT [counterterrorism], even CI [counterintelligence],
> believe it or not. So we took bodies from all these different divisions. We
> put them under one roof, so to speak. … And then we've added, of course, our
> partners at HSI [homeland security investigations, [which I detailed
> here](https://www.kenklippenstein.com/p/the-most-dangerous-feds-youve-
> never)], Department of Treasury, IRS, and we have them all sitting in the
> same space."

NSPM-7 directs the government to go after funders of Antifa, the left, and
general protest on the part of the American people. This in practice means
nonprofits and their donors.

Raia says that the Joint Mission Center is finding its footing:

> "So we've seen that mature over the last seven or eight months that I've
> been here from a concept to really starting to hit their stride and really
> starting to attack these entities that wanna do violence against the
> government, wanna do violence to the politicians."

The Center, Raia says, is ramping up its activity to investigate and bring
criminal charges against those engaged in "cyberstalking" and "interstate"
threats, known in the FBI as an "875" investigation because of a federal
criminal statute that prohibits transmitting threats, extortion, or ransom
demands. Applauding the willingness of U.S. Attorneys to bring charges against
social media posters, Raia says, "I gotta give kudos where kudos is due,"
remarking that it was impossible to get such a charge five years ago.

Here's how Raia put it:

> "Good luck trying to get an 875 charge from a US attorney, you know, five,
> 10 years ago. We're really getting a lot of support from our partners in DOJ
> and the US Attorney's Office in going after these folks. And whether it's a
> cyberstalking charge, whether it's 875 interstate threat charge -- really
> getting a lot of buy-in from the US Attorney's Office and putting a lot of
> these folks behind bars."

Anecdotally, I've heard of a lot of cases of people getting door-knocks for
spicy social media posts.

None of them have been charged with anything. Yet. Now that the Eagle is armed
though, the American symbol of freedom is getting its own thought-seeking
missile. We all know who is standing downrange.
